ann_24.text: This part of the model acts on 74 of the 345 training cases, and 3 of those 74 are actually 'yes'.
For the typical case it acts on (a1 = 2, a2 = 1, a3 = 1, a4 = 1, a5 = 3, a6 = 1), it clearly moves the predicted probability of 'yes' from above 99% without the part to below 1% with it.

Through this part, giving a2 or a4 its first value slightly lowers the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes', and for the typical case it acts on, moving a3 or a6 away from its first value slightly raises it, all staying below 1%.
Giving a5 the value 4 slightly lowers it too (on the training data only).
The effects of a2 and a4 through this part are also slightly larger when the other first values (a2, a3 or a6) are present.

ann_25.text: This part of the model reads only a4; through it, changing a4 from 2 to any other value raises the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes' from below 1% to about 47% (on the training data only).
It acts on 215 of the 345 training cases, and 67 of them are actually 'yes'.

For the typical case it acts on (a1 = 1, a2 = 3, a3 = 1, a4 = 3, a5 = 2, a6 = 1), it slightly raises the predicted probability of 'yes', from about 95% without the part to above 99% with it (on the training data only).

ann_26.text: This part of the model reads only a1; through it, a1 = 2 slightly lowers the predicted probability of 'yes' (on the training data only).

ann_27.text: This part of the model, which reads only a2, barely changes the predictions.
Through it, a2 other than 3 slightly lowers the predicted probability of 'yes' (on the training data only).

ann_28.text: Through this part, moving a5 away from its first value, to 2, 3 or 4, raises the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes' from below 1% to above 99%, and changing a2 from 3 to 1 raises it to about 22% (on the training data only).
Moving a3 away from its first value slightly lowers it.
Moving a1 away from its first value or changing a2 from 3 to 2 slightly raises it, and moving a6 away from its first value or giving a4 the value 3 slightly lowers it (on the training data only).

ann_29.text: For the typical case, moving a5 away from its first value, to 2, 3 or 4, raises the predicted probability of 'yes' from below 1% to above 99% (on the training data only).
Changing a4 from 2 to 3 slightly raises it, to about 1%, and changing a2 from 3 to 2 also slightly raises it.
Moving a1 away from its first value slightly raises it as well (on the training data only).

ann_24.original: An at-least-three-of-four first-value detector over attributes a2, a3, a4, a6 (a1 and a5 are not consulted, apart from a weak a5=4 term). In indicator terms the pre-activation is -24.87 + 11.00*I(a2=1) + 10.13*I(a3=1) + 11.97*I(a4=1) + 10.64*I(a6=1) + 2.43*I(a5=4) (a3 and a6 enter through their complements a3:2, a6:2 with negative weights). Any two indicators sum to at most 22.97 < 24.87, so with two indicators the unit is off except for a sliver (0.17 or 0.54) when a5=4 is also present; any three indicators sum to at least 31.77, so the unit fires at 6.9-18.9 whenever three or more of {a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} hold. Its -6.04 readout then drives the output logit far negative.
ann_24.proposed: This part acts on 74 training cases, 3 of them actually 'yes', and pushes their predicted probability of 'yes' from above 99% to below 1%; through it, first values of a2 and a4 slightly lower the predicted probability of 'yes' and a3 or a6 away from its first value slightly raises it.

ann_25.original: A binary gate on a4 != 2: h713 = 2.418 * I(a4 != 2) exactly (pre-activation -2.42 when a4=2). With readout +3.945 it adds +9.54 to the logit unless a4=2, i.e. a per-attribute penalty of 9.54 on a4=2. Because a4:2 has no direct edge, this is the only route by which a4=2 is distinguished from a4=1/3 in the linear part. EVIDENCE: closed form, train line plot (two levels, corr -1.00), mean-ablation flips 10% of train predictions.
ann_25.proposed: A switch on a4: any value other than 2 raises the predicted probability of 'yes' (to about 47% for the typical case, on the training data only).

ann_26.original: A ReLU unit that is always active on the domain, hence purely affine: h2408 = 0.526 + 2.801 I(a1=2). Its -0.578 readout contributes -0.304 - 1.619 I(a1=2), partly cancelling the direct a1:2 edge (+3.49): net a1=2 effect falls from +3.49 to +1.87 relative to a1 not 2. A redundant linear correction rather than a nonlinearity. EVIDENCE: closed form, train line plot (corr 1.00, always active), mean-ablation flips 3.2% of predictions.
ann_26.proposed: A small a1 term: a1 = 2 slightly lowers the predicted probability of 'yes' (on the training data only).

ann_27.original: A three-unit serial chain (NOT of NOT of a2=3) that re-encodes I(a2=3) and attenuates it: h951 = 0.138 - 0.0596 I(a2=3), so its logit contribution is -0.051 + 0.022 I(a2=3). Functionally near-inert vestigial structure: the effect is 0.022 logits against a direct a2=3 effect of -3.5. EVIDENCE: closed form, train line plot (two levels, corr -1.00), mean-ablation changes 1/345 train predictions.
ann_27.proposed: This part barely changes the predictions.

ann_28.original: The model's additive per-attribute score. Per-attribute contributions: a1=(1:-2.02, 2:+1.47, 3:+0.71); a2=(1:+4.84, 2:-1.31, 3:-3.52); a3=(1:+3.89, 2:-4.10); a4=(1:+1.30, 2:+1.30, 3:-2.85); a5=(1:-13.49, 2:+3.36, 3:+6.66, 4:+3.67); a6=(1:+4.74, 2:-5.00). It rewards first values of a2, a3, a6 (swings of 8-10 logits each) and weakly a4=1 vs a4=3, but carries a dominant veto on a5=1 (about -17 relative to other a5 values) and a mild penalty on a1=1 (-3). So it is not a symmetric count of first values: it is a count over a2/a3/a6 (a4 completed by the a4!=2 gate) with a strong a5=1 veto. EVIDENCE: closed form, train sensitivity (a5:1 largest at 7.30).
ann_28.proposed: An additive score in which a5 away from its first value raises the predicted probability of 'yes' to above 99% and a2 = 1 raises it to about 22% for the typical case (on the training data only), with small effects of a1, a3, a4 and a6.

ann_29.original: Additive composition under the output sigmoid: logit = -0.213 + Linear + 3.945*A4gate - 6.037*Count3of4 - 0.578*A1unit - 0.370*A2chain, i.e. in indicator terms Linear + 9.54 I(a4!=2) - 6.04 G - 1.62 I(a1=2) + 0.022 I(a2=3) - 0.57, with G the at-least-three-of-{a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} gate. Mechanism: (1) Count3of4 is a veto: whenever k4 = #{a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} >= 3 it subtracts at least 41.7 logits and the model predicts class 0 (0/84 configs positive). (2) Otherwise the sign is set by the linear score plus the a4!=2 bonus: a5=1 contributes about -17 relative to the other a5 values and vetoes almost everything (1/87 a5=1 configs with k4<3 positive); with a5!=1, k4=0 is mostly negative (6/36 positive) and k4 in {1,2} is almost always positive (211/225). So the network approximates 'a5 != 1 AND one or two of {a2,a3,a4,a6} take their first value' (agreement 95.1% over all 432 configurations, 94.8% of train rows). a1:1 (node -1) has no enabled edges and is a zero-effect entry; a1 matters only through the direct a1:2/a1:3 terms and the affine a1:2 unit. The two minor children are linear/near-constant corrections (mean-ablation changes 3.2% and 0.3% of train predictions); the count gate is the dominant nonlinearity (mean-ablation flips 52%). EVIDENCE: composed closed form (sigmoid of the weighted sum of children); exhaustive enumeration over 432 configurations; train performance of the composed model accuracy 0.655, AUC 0.766 (identical to the evolved network). Relative to the MONK-2 target (exactly two of six first values), the network ignores a1=1, treats a5=1 as a veto instead of a counted indicator, and counts only a2,a3,a4,a6, so it fires for one OR two first values among those four.
ann_29.proposed: For the typical case the model turns to 'yes' when a5 moves away from its first value (on the training data only); a4 = 3, a2 = 2 and a1 away from its first value raise the predicted probability of 'yes' only slightly.

summary.text: For the typical case (the most common value of each attribute: a1 = 1, a2 = 3, a3 = 1, a4 = 2, a5 = 1, a6 = 1), moving a5 away from its first value, to 2, 3 or 4, raises the predicted probability of 'yes' from below 1% to above 99% (on the training data only).
One part of the model acts on 74 of the 345 training cases, and 3 of those 74 are actually 'yes'.
For the typical case this part acts on (a1 = 2, a2 = 1, a3 = 1, a4 = 1, a5 = 3, a6 = 1), it clearly moves the predicted probability of 'yes' from above 99% without the part to below 1% with it.
Through another part, changing a4 from 2 to any other value raises the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes' from below 1% to about 47% (on the training data only).
In the model as a whole, changing a4 from 2 to 3 slightly raises it, to about 1%, and changing a2 from 3 to 2 also slightly raises it.
One small part of the model, which reads only a2, barely changes the predictions.

worth_checking.text: Worth checking: through one part the model separates a4 = 2 from every other value of a4, including the first, raising the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes' to about 47% when a4 is not 2 (on the training data only), and in the model as a whole a4 = 3 gets a slightly higher one than a4 = 2.

parts.name: a5_veto_count_peak_model
parts.original_hypothesis: Additive composition under the output sigmoid: logit = -0.213 + Linear + 3.945*A4gate - 6.037*Count3of4 - 0.578*A1unit - 0.370*A2chain, i.e. in indicator terms Linear + 9.54 I(a4!=2) - 6.04 G - 1.62 I(a1=2) + 0.022 I(a2=3) - 0.57, with G the at-least-three-of-{a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} gate. Mechanism: (1) Count3of4 is a veto: whenever k4 = #{a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} >= 3 it subtracts at least 41.7 logits and the model predicts class 0 (0/84 configs positive). (2) Otherwise the sign is set by the linear score plus the a4!=2 bonus: a5=1 contributes about -17 relative to the other a5 values and vetoes almost everything (1/87 a5=1 configs with k4<3 positive); with a5!=1, k4=0 is mostly negative (6/36 positive) and k4 in {1,2} is almost always positive (211/225). So the network approximates 'a5 != 1 AND one or two of {a2,a3,a4,a6} take their first value' (agreement 95.1% over all 432 configurations, 94.8% of train rows). a1:1 (node -1) has no enabled edges and is a zero-effect entry; a1 matters only through the direct a1:2/a1:3 terms and the affine a1:2 unit. The two minor children are linear/near-constant corrections (mean-ablation changes 3.2% and 0.3% of train predictions); the count gate is the dominant nonlinearity (mean-ablation flips 52%). EVIDENCE: composed closed form (sigmoid of the weighted sum of children); exhaustive enumeration over 432 configurations; train performance of the composed model accuracy 0.655, AUC 0.766 (identical to the evolved network). Relative to the MONK-2 target (exactly two of six first values), the network ignores a1=1, treats a5=1 as a veto instead of a counted indicator, and counts only a2,a3,a4,a6, so it fires for one OR two first values among those four.

parts.name: count_gate_3of4
parts.original_hypothesis: An at-least-three-of-four first-value detector over attributes a2, a3, a4, a6 (a1 and a5 are not consulted, apart from a weak a5=4 term). In indicator terms the pre-activation is -24.87 + 11.00*I(a2=1) + 10.13*I(a3=1) + 11.97*I(a4=1) + 10.64*I(a6=1) + 2.43*I(a5=4) (a3 and a6 enter through their complements a3:2, a6:2 with negative weights). Any two indicators sum to at most 22.97 < 24.87, so with two indicators the unit is off except for a sliver (0.17 or 0.54) when a5=4 is also present; any three indicators sum to at least 31.77, so the unit fires at 6.9-18.9 whenever three or more of {a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} hold. Its -6.04 readout then drives the output logit far negative.

parts.name: direct_linear_terms
parts.original_hypothesis: The model's additive per-attribute score. Per-attribute contributions: a1=(1:-2.02, 2:+1.47, 3:+0.71); a2=(1:+4.84, 2:-1.31, 3:-3.52); a3=(1:+3.89, 2:-4.10); a4=(1:+1.30, 2:+1.30, 3:-2.85); a5=(1:-13.49, 2:+3.36, 3:+6.66, 4:+3.67); a6=(1:+4.74, 2:-5.00). It rewards first values of a2, a3, a6 (swings of 8-10 logits each) and weakly a4=1 vs a4=3, but carries a dominant veto on a5=1 (about -17 relative to other a5 values) and a mild penalty on a1=1 (-3). So it is not a symmetric count of first values: it is a count over a2/a3/a6 (a4 completed by the a4!=2 gate) with a strong a5=1 veto. EVIDENCE: closed form, train sensitivity (a5:1 largest at 7.30).

parts.name: a4_not2_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: A binary gate on a4 != 2: h713 = 2.418 * I(a4 != 2) exactly (pre-activation -2.42 when a4=2). With readout +3.945 it adds +9.54 to the logit unless a4=2, i.e. a per-attribute penalty of 9.54 on a4=2. Because a4:2 has no direct edge, this is the only route by which a4=2 is distinguished from a4=1/3 in the linear part. EVIDENCE: closed form, train line plot (two levels, corr -1.00), mean-ablation flips 10% of train predictions.

parts.name: a1_2_linear_unit
parts.original_hypothesis: A ReLU unit that is always active on the domain, hence purely affine: h2408 = 0.526 + 2.801 I(a1=2). Its -0.578 readout contributes -0.304 - 1.619 I(a1=2), partly cancelling the direct a1:2 edge (+3.49): net a1=2 effect falls from +3.49 to +1.87 relative to a1 not 2. A redundant linear correction rather than a nonlinearity. EVIDENCE: closed form, train line plot (corr 1.00, always active), mean-ablation flips 3.2% of predictions.

parts.name: a2_3_double_negation_chain
parts.original_hypothesis: A three-unit serial chain (NOT of NOT of a2=3) that re-encodes I(a2=3) and attenuates it: h951 = 0.138 - 0.0596 I(a2=3), so its logit contribution is -0.051 + 0.022 I(a2=3). Functionally near-inert vestigial structure: the effect is 0.022 logits against a direct a2=3 effect of -3.5. EVIDENCE: closed form, train line plot (two levels, corr -1.00), mean-ablation changes 1/345 train predictions.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording
